prerequisites: Basic competencies in Mathematics and Informatics
Modeling and Control of Continuous Systems

learning_outcomes.text: Students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds on general secondary education, and is typically at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects involving knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.

Students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional manner and possess the competences typically demonstrated by developing and defending arguments and solving problems within their field of study.
Basic knowledge of the profession.
Ability to use ICT.
Problem-solving capacity.
Knowledge and ability for system modeling and simulation.
Knowledge of automatic regulation and control techniques and their application to industrial automation.
Ability to design industrial control and automation systems.
Linear discrete-time dynamic systems.
Analysis of discrete-time dynamic systems.
Design of discrete-time control systems.
Real-time systems.
Design of real-time control systems.
Design of algorithms in concurrent language.
Understand and know how to apply design and implementation methods for discrete-time system control.
Understand and know how to apply design and implementation methods for real-time control systems.
Understand the concept of discrete-time systems and sampled systems from the perspective of control engineering design.
Analyze the temporal response of linear systems, with and without feedback, in discrete time.
Discretize continuous PID controllers.
Design discrete-time controllers based on external description (transfer function).
Implement controllers in microprocessor-based systems.
Understand the concepts of cyclic executive scheduling, concurrent tasks, synchronization, and mutual exclusion in real-time systems.
Master at least one modeling method and one programming language for their application in real-time systems.
Scheduling and implementation of real-time control systems.

teaching_methods: Lectures/participatory classes for each theoretical topic.
Exercise solving and demonstrations with interactive and industrial tools.
Assimilation of knowledge from theoretical classes.
Solving exercises proposed in lectures/participatory classes.
Solving practical cases proposed in laboratory practicals.
Preparation of reports for exercise sets and laboratory practicals.
assessment_rules: The final grade for the ordinary call is calculated as: 0.3 * laboratory practical reports + 0.6 * theoretical-practical exam + 0.1 * participation. A minimum grade of 5 points (out of 10) is required for each of the two practical reports and each of the two parts of the theoretical-practical exam. Participation credit is only added if all other activities are passed. For the extraordinary call, students who did not submit practical reports will take a laboratory exam (30% weight) and have a personal interview with the teaching team (10% weight), instead of the reports and participation. For single assessment, a laboratory exam (30%) and personal interview (10%) replace reports and participation. In all cases, a minimum grade of 5 in each assessed part is required for the entire course to be considered passed.
